v: He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had his hand withered.
They watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
He said to the man who had his hand withered, “Stand up.”
He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?” But they were silent.

When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.”  He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
b: This passage describes a miracle Jesus performed when he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath: he healed a man with a withered hand. This provoked the Pharisees, who held that healing on the Sabbath was unlawful. But Jesus made it clear that the Sabbath was made for the good of people, and in this way he challenged the religious leaders' view of the law.

Jesus did more than perform a healing miracle. He used the occasion to teach a deeper truth: the Sabbath is for doing good and saving life, not for keeping a rigid rule. His act exposed the hardness of the Pharisees' hearts and their resistance to the truth, an attitude that finally led them to plot to destroy Jesus.

Through this passage God shows us his kindness and compassion. He will not stop doing good and saving because of the limits of the law. Jesus teaches us that true worship and obedience lie in uprightness of heart and love, not merely in outward observance of the law. This passage reminds us how we should act in love in our lives, rather than being bound by the law.
q: In daily life, have you ever clung to certain rules or traditions and neglected a genuine act of love? How will you act in love in place of rigid legalism?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us, through Jesus Christ, true love and compassion. Help us to go beyond the limits of the law and learn to honor you with love and good deeds. May our hearts no longer be hard but soft, sensitive to your guidance, and may we put your teaching into practice in our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples, and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.
He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.
For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.
The unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, “You are the Son of God!”
He sternly warned them that they should not make him known.
b: This passage records how Jesus' ministry in Galilee gradually expanded and drew large crowds. Hearing of his miracles, people hurried from every region to seek his healing and help. Concerned that the crowd pressing in would hinder his work, Jesus had his disciples prepare a small boat for him in case it was needed.

It is worth noting that when the unclean spirits saw Jesus, they immediately recognized him as the Son of God and fell down before him. But Jesus ordered them not to make him known. This command shows Jesus' control over his mission. He knew his time had not yet come and that he needed to act carefully, so as not to provoke premature hostility or misunderstanding.

Through this passage God tells us that Jesus' ministry was always full of compassion and wisdom. He healed the sick and drove out unclean spirits, but he also knew how to guard his mission so as to finish his work at the proper time. This reminds us that in our lives and ministries we also need to act wisely, understanding when to be open and when to hold back, so that we walk within God's will.
q: In your present circumstances, is there any area that needs wisdom and discernment? How do you rely on God's guidance in these situations to make fitting choices?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Jesus Christ, how to act in love and to face life's challenges wisely. Give us the wisdom to discern, so that we know when to act and when to wait, and may we do everything according to your will. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He went up into the mountain, and called to himself those whom he wanted, and they went to him.
He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach,
and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:
Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);
James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);
Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Then he came into a house.
b: This passage records how Jesus chose twelve disciples and gave them authority. Jesus chose these disciples as he himself desired and appointed them to be with him, not only to learn but to experience a life of walking with the Lord. Their mission was not only to follow Jesus but to be sent out to preach, and they were given authority to cast out demons, so that by God's power they could overcome the forces of darkness and proclaim the power of the gospel.

Jesus' choice and appointment of each disciple shows his knowledge of them and his expectations for them. He gave Simon a new name, "Peter," meaning "rock," symbolizing firmness of faith. James and John were called "Sons of Thunder," showing their passionate and courageous character. These names were more than labels; they represented the roles and missions they would have in God's kingdom.

Through this passage God reveals a profound truth to us: he calls us to come to him, to be with him, and gives us authority to carry out his mission. Whatever our background or personality, God knows us and shapes us, making us vessels in his hands to serve his kingdom. Like these disciples, we need to lay down ourselves, submit to the Lord's leading, and faithfully complete the task God entrusts to us.
q: The Lord Jesus is also calling us to take part in his work. Are you willing to lay down yourself and faithfully complete the mission God has entrusted to you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for calling us to be your beloved disciples. Help us to be willing to lay down ourselves, follow the Lord Jesus wholeheartedly, and faithfully complete the mission you have given us. Give us wisdom and courage, so that by your authority we may face life's challenges and spread your gospel. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
When his friends heard it, they went out to seize him; for they said, “He is insane.”
The scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”
He summoned them, and said to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.
But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.
Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;
but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
—because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
b: This passage describes the misunderstanding and attack Jesus faced in his ministry. His relatives thought he was out of his mind, while the scribes accused him of casting out demons by the power of the prince of demons. Jesus answered these accusations with parables, pointing out that a kingdom or a house divided against itself cannot stand. He went on to say that Satan does not fight against himself, and that his power to cast out demons came from God's authority, not from Satan's power.

In this passage Jesus stresses the seriousness of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, a sin that cannot be forgiven. He warns those who misunderstood and slandered him: to attribute his works to Satan is a grave blasphemy against the work of the Holy Spirit.

Through this passage God teaches us to be careful in what we say and do, and not to judge God's work lightly, especially when we do not understand it. We should hold a heart of reverence and seek God's wisdom and guidance, rather than slander or misunderstand carelessly.
q: When you face spiritual experiences that are hard to understand, how do you seek God's guidance and wisdom? In such situations, are you willing to lay down your own judgment and trust God completely?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Jesus Christ, how to discern your works. Give us wisdom and a humble heart, so that we can understand rightly and respond to your work in our lives. Help us not to criticize or misjudge others lightly, but to focus on your truth and love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.
A multitude was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters are outside looking for you.”
He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and mother.”
b: In this passage Jesus' mother and brothers came looking for him, and he used the occasion to explain the idea of the spiritual family to the crowd. He said that whoever does the will of God is his mother, brother, and sister. These words do not deny the relationships of his earthly family, but stress the importance of spiritual kinship in God's kingdom.

Jesus reminds us that as Christians we are not only family by natural blood but also a spiritual family, because we are united with one another in Christ. Our spiritual family is built on doing God's will, a relationship that even goes beyond earthly blood ties.
Through this passage God reminds us to treasure and nurture spiritual relationships. Spiritual kinship is centered on God's will, and when we do his will we enter this heavenly family.
q: In your life, how do you view and care for your spiritual family relationships? Is there any place where spiritual kinship needs to be strengthened?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for making us a spiritual family in Christ. Help us to value and nurture these spiritual relationships more, so that in doing your will we support one another and love one another. May our lives reflect your love and truth and be a witness to your kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea, and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,
“Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow,
and as he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
Others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
b: In this passage Jesus teaches the crowd with the parable of the sower, describing God's word as seed sown on different kinds of soil, where the nature of the soil determines how the seed grows and bears fruit. Seed that fell beside the road was eaten by birds, representing those who hear the word but do not understand it, and Satan takes it away. Seed that fell on rocky ground withered for lack of root, symbolizing people of weak faith who cannot endure. Seed that fell among thorns was choked, representing those who lose the fruit of faith to worldly cares and the deceitfulness of riches. Finally, only seed that fell on good soil could grow and bear fruit, producing an abundant harvest.

This parable reminds us that the growth of faith depends on our heart's attitude toward God's word. If, like the good soil, we receive God's word with a humble and obedient heart, we will see the fruit of faith gradually appear in our lives, bringing a harvest of thirty, sixty, even a hundredfold.

Through this passage God reminds us that each of us has the potential to be "good soil." The key is whether we have prepared the field of our hearts to receive his word and to put his word into practice in our lives. Jesus' teaching encourages us to be good soil heavy with fruit, letting God's word sprout and bear fruit within us and bring eternal value.
q: Is the field of your heart prepared to receive God's word? In daily life, how can you become "good soil," letting God's word sprout and grow in your heart and bear abundant fruit?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for sowing your precious word in our hearts. Make our hearts like good soil, able to receive your truth humbly and take deep root in it, shielded from worldly influence, and bearing good fruit in our lives. May our lives glorify you and show your love and grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.
He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,
that ‘seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’ ”
He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
The farmer sows the word.
The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes, and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.
They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,
and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
b: In this passage Jesus explains the parable of the sower to help his disciples understand the mystery of God's kingdom. Jesus' teaching reveals the different attitudes people have toward God's word and describes four kinds of hearts. First, the heart beside the road represents those who hear the word but do not understand, and Satan quickly takes it away. Second, the rocky heart symbolizes believers who have a moment of enthusiasm for God's word but lack roots, and who easily fall when trouble comes. Third, the heart among thorns refers to those who are squeezed by worldly cares, riches, and desires so that they cannot bear fruit. Finally, the good-soil heart symbolizes those who are willing to listen, receive, and bear abundant fruit.

Through this parable Jesus reminds us that the quality of the soil of our hearts determines our relationship with God's word. A faith that truly bears fruit needs a prepared heart, one that can not only hear God's word but also let it root deeply and live out a witness. A good-soil heart is not disturbed by the world but focuses on God's word, and this is how it produces an abundant harvest.

Through this passage God reminds us that to become good soil, we need to clear the stones and thorns from our hearts and let God's word grow freely within us. Only when we focus on God's kingdom and let go of worldly worries and deceptions can we truly bear fruit thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.
q: What "stones" or "thorns" in your life need to be removed so that God's word can bear more fruit? How are you willing to adjust yourself so that God's word takes root and bears fruit in your heart?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through this parable how to become good soil. Help us to remove the worries and temptations in our hearts, so that your word may take root, grow, and bear fruit in us. May our lives be a witness to your kingdom and bring abundant spiritual fruit. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to them, “Is the lamp brought to be put under a basket  or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?
For there is nothing hidden, except that it should be made known; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.
If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”
He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be given to you who hear.
For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”
b: In this passage Jesus uses the picture of a lamp to teach his disciples, reminding them that the light of faith cannot be hidden, just as a lit lamp should be placed on a stand to give light to everyone around. Jesus' teaching shows that his truth will certainly come to light, and even if it seems hidden at first, it will in the end shine on all darkness. The mission of believers is to make God's word openly known, so that through the witness of our lives the world may see it and be influenced.

Jesus then stresses, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear!" This calls us not only to hear God's word but to receive it carefully and attentively and to put it into practice in our lives. This listening is not superficial reception; it means reflecting with a humble heart and turning what we hear into action, living out the power of the truth. He goes on to say, "With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you," reminding us to show kindness in the way we treat others, because we will be repaid according to how we treat them. God wants us to have broad hearts and to give gladly, and he will bless us many times over.

Finally Jesus says, "For whoever has, to him will be given, and whoever doesn't have, from him will be taken away even that which he has." This describes the law of growth in spiritual life: those who wholeheartedly receive God's word will gain more wisdom and revelation, while those who are unwilling to open their hearts to the truth will gradually lose even the light of faith they have. God's truth is an abundant spring. If we thirst for him and seek him, we will receive more spiritual growth; if we are indifferent to the truth, we will miss his grace.

Through this passage God reminds us that the light of faith cannot be hidden but must be put in a prominent place for the world to see. Our lives should be a witness to God's word, sharing his love and truth. As we keep living out God's word, he will bless us many times over, making us richer and more influential.
q: Where in your life does God's light need to shine more? Are you willing to share God's word with others, so that your faith becomes a lamp in their eyes?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us the light of truth. Help us to live out our faith boldly and let your light shine on this world. Make our hearts soft, willing to listen to and obey your word, and to share your love with those around us. May our lives be a witness to your kingdom and draw more people to know you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.
For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
b: In this passage Jesus uses a parable of seed to describe how God's kingdom grows. The parable shows how God's kingdom grows without our noticing, stressing that God's works often go beyond our understanding. Once the sower has sown the seed, night and day pass and the seed sprouts and grows by itself, finally bearing abundant fruit. This process does not depend on the sower's wisdom or skill, but on God's creative power and provision.

By saying, "The earth bears fruit by itself," Jesus describes the mystery of God's kingdom, showing that it is not controlled by human hands but that God governs behind the scenes. This process of life is like the growth of faith, which takes time, patience, and complete dependence on God. Though we do not fully understand how this growth happens, as long as we faithfully sow and wait, God will bring the fruit to ripeness at the right time and bring a season of harvest.

Through this passage God reminds us not to focus too much on our own efforts in the growth of faith, but to trust his work. He governs our spiritual growth, and even when we see no obvious change, he is still quietly accomplishing his plan in our hearts. As long as we are willing to sow seeds of faith and work faithfully, we will in the end see his grace on the day of harvest.
q: Is there anything in your life that calls for more patience in waiting for God to accomplish it? Are you willing to trust his plan and faithfully sow seeds of faith at every stage of life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for working quietly in our lives so that we keep growing in faith. Give us patience and faith to trust your plan and your timing, and to faithfully sow seeds of love and faith. May our lives bear spiritual fruit and glorify your holy name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.
b: In this passage Jesus uses the mustard seed to describe the kingdom of God. The mustard seed is one of the smallest seeds on earth. It symbolizes that God's kingdom, though small and unremarkable at the start, once planted grows quickly and surpasses other plants, becoming a tall and strong tree that gives the birds of the sky a place to nest. This picture vividly presents the character of God's kingdom: small at first, yet holding immense potential, and in the end becoming a place of rest that embraces all things.

Jesus used this parable to help his disciples understand the power of God's kingdom and the way it spreads. God's kingdom does not depend on human strength but on God's own power, so that it grows naturally and brings influence. This also shows that the service and witness of each one of us, however insignificant it may seem, will be used by God if we offer it faithfully, and he will accomplish great works through these small efforts.

Through this passage God reminds us that even if our faith and service seem small, as long as we are willing to entrust them to him, they can bear fruit beyond imagination. God's kingdom takes root and sprouts in each of our hearts. We must persevere and plant our small faith, and God will make it grow strong by his great power and become part of his kingdom.
q: Are there small seeds of faith in your life waiting for God to make them grow? Are you willing to entrust these small bits of faith to God and believe that he will make them an abundant harvest?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see that your kingdom brings forth greatness out of smallness. Give us faith, so that in whatever situation we face we may firmly believe you will accomplish works beyond what we imagine. Help us to faithfully sow seeds of faith, and let your kingdom keep expanding in our hearts and lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up, and told him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
They were greatly afraid, and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
b: 在這段經文中，我們看到耶穌和門徒們在湖上遇到一場突如其來的風暴。當波浪湧進船內，門徒們被恐懼所支配，認為自己的生命即將失去，便驚慌地叫醒耶穌。然而，耶穌在混亂之中卻安然地在船尾睡覺，顯示出祂的從容與信心。當耶穌醒來後，祂斥責風浪，並平靜了海面，使湖面恢復安寧。
耶穌隨後對門徒說：「為甚麼膽怯？你們還沒有信心嗎？」祂指出門徒們在風暴中缺乏信心，提醒他們即使面對困難，也應當堅信祂的能力和愛。這段經文教導我們，即使在生命的風暴中，我們的主也掌管一切。耶穌那超然的平靜成為信心的榜樣，顯示出祂在困境中與我們同在，並有能力勝過任何環境。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，無論我們遇到多大的風浪，都不要驚慌，因為耶穌與我們同在，祂能帶來平安。我們的信心不應建立在外在環境的安穩，而是在耶穌的話語與同在上。只要我們倚靠祂，無論面對多大的風暴，祂都能平靜我們的心靈，使我們安穩地渡過。
q: 當生命遇到風浪時，您是否能夠依靠耶穌的同在而不再害怕？您如何在面對挑戰時建立對祂的信心，使祂成為您安穩的力量？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您在風暴中與我們同在，並賜給我們平安的力量。求您增強我們的信心，使我們在挑戰中依然穩固地信靠您，不再膽怯。願您的話語成為我們的支柱，使我們在困難面前堅持不懈，經歷您奇妙的同在。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.
He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,
because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.
Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,
and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”
For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.
All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”
At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.
Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.
They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.
Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
They began to beg him to depart from their region.
As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”
He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.
b: 這段經文中，耶穌顯示了祂驚人的能力，戰勝了惡勢力，使被污鬼附著的人得自由。這位受苦的男子因被群鬼纏繞，無法過正常生活，甚至被孤立在墳塋中，無人能夠幫助他。但耶穌的到來成為他命運的轉折點，祂將群鬼趕出，使男子得著真正的自由和平安。這不僅展現出耶穌掌權於所有靈界勢力，更顯示出祂對受苦之人的憐憫。
經文中，群鬼懇求耶穌准許他們附於豬群中，並隨即帶來大範圍的影響，豬群紛紛投海而死。這件事引起了城中居民的恐懼，他們因無法理解耶穌的能力和祂行事的方式，而懇求祂離開。然而，那曾被群鬼所附之人卻因得救而變得清醒、平靜，並願意跟隨耶穌。儘管耶穌沒有允許他跟隨，但祂卻給了這人新的使命，要他將神的恩典和救贖之愛傳揚開來。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，祂有能力釋放我們脫離任何困難與束縛，無論是外在的壓力還是內心的掙扎，耶穌都願意介入並拯救。我們在祂裡面能夠找到真正的自由和平安，並且成為祂恩典的見證人，向他人分享祂的偉大作為，帶領更多人歸向祂。
q: 您是否曾經在生命中經歷過神的釋放？有什麼見證可以分享，以幫助他人認識神的能力和憐憫？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜給我們自由的恩典，使我們得以從捆綁中得釋放。求您幫助我們在耶穌基督裡得著平安與安息，並賜給我們勇氣去見證您在我們生命中的奇妙作為，讓更多人看見您的愛與大能。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,
and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”
He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.
b: 在這段經文中，我們見證了耶穌如何在面對睚魯的求助時，顯示出祂的憐憫和神聖能力。睚魯，作為會堂的管事，面對女兒的病危，他帶著迫切的信心來到耶穌面前，求祂按手使女兒痊癒。耶穌聽見他的呼求，立刻同意前往。途中雖然有人告訴睚魯女兒已經死了，但耶穌卻說：「不要怕，只要信！」這句話鼓勵我們在困境中保持信心，無論情況多麼絕望，只要信靠神，祂的能力就能改變一切。
耶穌來到睚魯家時，家中充滿了哀哭聲。祂宣告女孩只是「睡著了」，這一宣告挑戰了對死亡的認識。耶穌將嘲笑祂的人撵出房間，然後拉著女孩的手，對她說：「大利大，古米！」女孩立刻復甦，這神蹟使所有人驚奇不已。耶穌的行動不僅顯示了祂對生命和死亡的掌控，也讓我們看見神的應許和能力在我們的生命中是如何彰顯的。
這段經文提醒我們，無論我們面臨什麼挑戰或困境，耶穌的能力和愛始終能夠改變現狀。當我們在困難中感到無助時，耶穌的話語是我們的力量來源。祂鼓勵我們在絕望中保持信心，相信神的計劃和應許，因為神的能力超越我們的理解和期待。當我們堅持信靠祂，祂必定能夠帶來轉變和希望。
q: 在您的生活中，您目前面臨哪些挑戰？如何能在這些困境中增強信心，相信神的應許，並依靠祂的力量來面對挑戰？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌基督，彰顯了您的憐憫和能力。當我們面對困難和挑戰時，求您幫助我們全心信靠您，知道您能夠帶來改變和希望。願我們在每一個挑戰中見證您的大能，並以堅定的信心依靠您。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: A certain woman, who had a discharge of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.
For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”
Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’ ”
He looked around to see her who had done this thing.
But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
b: 這段經文描述了一位長期患病的婦人如何在耶穌的醫治下得到釋放。她因為血漏病而受到極大的痛苦和困擾，並且花光了所有的積蓄卻無法醫治。在她聽到耶穌的事後，心中充滿信心，決定觸摸耶穌的衣裳，以期得著醫治。她的信心得到了回應，病情立刻得到改善，血漏乾了。
耶穌感受到能力從自己身上出去，知道有人觸摸了他的衣裳。即使在擁擠的人群中，耶穌依然關心那位婦人的需要。當婦人因恐懼和顫抖站在耶穌面前，將事情的真相告訴他時，耶穌對她說：「你的信救了你。」這句話不僅表達了對她信心的肯定，也顯示了耶穌的醫治力量和對她的愛。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，真正的信心能夠使我們得到神的醫治和幫助。即使我們面對困難和挑戰，只要我們信靠耶穌，尋求祂的幫助，祂必定會在我們的生命中彰顯祂的大能。
q: 在您的生命中，有哪些地方您需要依靠神的力量來得著醫治或改變？您如何能夠像這位婦人一樣，展現真正的信心，並經歷神的祝福？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌基督，讓我們看到信心的力量。求您幫助我們在面對困難時，能夠全心信靠您，尋求您的幫助。願我們的信心如同這位婦人一般堅定，並經歷您的醫治和祝福。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.

When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?
Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” They were offended at him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people, and healed them.
He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.
b: 這段經文記錄了耶穌回到家鄉的經歷，然而，家鄉的人因為熟悉他的背景，反而輕視他。當耶穌在會堂中教訓時，人們不僅質疑他的智慧和能力，還提到他的木匠身份與家族背景，因為這些原因，他們不願意相信耶穌的身份，甚至對他產生排斥之心。這段經文凸顯了人的成見如何影響對真理的接受，讓人失去領受恩典的機會。
耶穌的回應「大凡先知，除了本地、親屬、本家之外，沒有不被人尊敬的」，顯示了在熟悉的環境中，最難被接納的是先知的身份，因為親近的人往往因為成見，而看不見神的工作。這也提醒我們，過於依賴過去的認知，容易讓我們忽略神在當下的作為和恩典。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，信心和敞開的心是我們領受神工作的基礎。如果我們心中帶有偏見或成見，就可能阻礙神在我們生命中行神蹟。我們應時刻保持謙卑、敞開的心，去領受神的教導和改變，超越我們所見和所知，並且相信神在我們的生命中擁有最好的計劃。
q: 在您熟悉的環境或人際關係中，有哪些成見或偏見阻礙了您對神作為的信心？您願意怎樣改變自己，以更開放的心迎接神的帶領？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您讓我們看到信心與謙卑的重要。求您幫助我們在熟悉的環境中，依然對您的作為保持開放的心，願我們不因偏見或成見而錯失您的恩典。求您加添我們的信心，使我們能看見您在我們生命中的帶領與祝福。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.
b: 這段經文描述了耶穌差派十二個門徒出去傳道的過程。他們受命帶著極少的物品，甚至沒有食物和金錢，唯有一根柺杖，表明他們完全依靠神的供應和保護。耶穌賜給他們權柄，可以制伏污鬼，並囑咐他們要簡單而信靠地生活。門徒的行動不僅僅是傳遞福音的言語，更是依靠神恩典的見證，讓人看到福音的真實性和力量。
耶穌要求門徒在傳道時「進了人的家就住在那裡」，提醒我們福音的傳遞需要穩定和長期的關係，而不是匆忙和草率。同時，祂也教導門徒若遭遇拒絕，要「把腳上的塵土跺下去」，不受那裡的不信所影響，繼續前行。這教導我們不應執著於被拒絕，應該堅持傳福音的使命，不讓挫折攔阻神的計劃。
上帝藉這段經文提醒我們，傳福音的重點在於信靠祂的供應和權柄，而非物質的預備。我們無需倚靠世俗的力量，只需帶著信心與簡樸的心去服事。當我們忠實地完成使命時，神會在我們身上彰顯祂的恩典與大能，並醫治、釋放那需要的人。
q: 當您在生活中面對傳福音的機會時，您是否願意簡樸依靠神，而非依賴自己的準備？您在面對拒絕時，是否能夠不受影響，繼續忠實於主的使命？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您差派我們成為您福音的使者，並賜給我們能力去傳揚您的愛。求您幫助我們學習依靠您，放下世俗的依賴，單單仰望您的供應與帶領。求您賜給我們勇氣，即使遭遇拒絕也不退縮，堅持為您作見證。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”
But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.
For John said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,
for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.
When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
He swore to her, “Whatever you shall ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
She went out, and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
She came in immediately with haste to the king, and asked, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”
The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths, and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.
Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring John’s head, and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.
When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
b: 這段經文記述了施洗約翰的殉道過程，以及希律王因驕傲和自負而犯下的可怕過失。約翰因直言不諱地指責希律不道德的行為而被監禁，但希律卻心中敬畏他，知他為義人，並對他的話感到動容。然而，因為希律的承諾和對名聲的顧忌，最終卻為了維護虛假的面子，草率地答應了希羅底的女兒，間接致使約翰被處死。
這段經文提醒我們，驕傲和不願意承認錯誤會帶來不可逆轉的後果。希律的心中雖有對約翰的敬重，但他仍選擇讓自己的名聲和面子凌駕於道德之上。人若不願意順從內心的敬畏與真理，最終會落入罪的網羅，甚至做出自己後悔的決定。
上帝藉著施洗約翰的忠誠見證，提醒我們在面對不義之事時，要堅守信仰，不隨波逐流。即便需要付出代價，真理永遠比一時的面子或虛榮更為珍貴。
q: 當您面臨到不義或壓力時，是否能夠勇敢地堅持真理？是否會因顧忌他人的眼光或面子而妥協，甚至做出自己不願的選擇？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜給我們施洗約翰的榜樣，提醒我們勇敢面對不義，無論環境多艱難，仍堅持真理。求您給我們力量，不被世俗的虛榮和驕傲所迷惑，讓我們的生命為您作見證，彰顯您的公義。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.
He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.
Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him, and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.
Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give them something to eat?”
He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate, and were filled.
They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.
Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
b: 這段經文記載了耶穌在曠野中餵飽五千人的神蹟。門徒們將所做的事和教導報告給耶穌，耶穌看到眾人的需要，憐憫他們，便教訓他們，並且在天色已晚時，顯示出祂的大能。門徒們提出眾人缺乏食物的問題，耶穌要求他們提供現有的食物，並用五個餅和兩條魚行了神蹟，讓眾人吃飽，還有剩餘的餅。
這個神蹟不僅顯示了耶穌的憐憫，也顯示了祂的能力和供應。即使面對看似不可能的困境，耶穌依然能夠滿足人們的需要。這也提醒我們，在面對困難時，應當將問題交託給神，相信祂會提供所需的資源。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，神的供應遠超過我們的需求，祂的能力無所不在。我們應該學習將困難和需求交託給神，並且相信祂能夠以意想不到的方式滿足我們的需要。
q: 當您面對資源不足或困難時，如何能夠相信神的供應和能力，並且學會交託您的困難給祂？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您在我們生活中的供應和保守。求您幫助我們在面對困難時，將問題交託給您，並且相信您的供應和能力。願我們在每一次的挑戰中，都能夠見證您的大能和恩典。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.
After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.
When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea,  and he would have passed by them,
but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
for they all saw him, and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them, and said to them, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;
for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
b: 這段經文記載了耶穌在海面上行走的神蹟，祂選擇在門徒遭遇風浪時前來，彰顯祂對門徒的關心與保護。當門徒因風浪而艱難前行時，耶穌並沒有立刻干預，而是在他們最需要的時刻來到身邊，以超乎常人的方式安慰並拯救他們。然而，門徒因著心中的恐懼，未能立刻認出祂，甚至誤以為是鬼怪。耶穌溫柔地安慰他們，「你們放心！是我，不要怕！」
耶穌的出現帶來了平安，當祂上了船後，風浪便立即止住。這段經文也提醒我們，門徒雖然見證了神蹟，卻仍未完全理解耶穌的能力與同在。這也反映了人心中的疑惑與愚頑，雖然經歷了神的恩典，卻常常因困境而懷疑神的保護。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，祂的同在無所不在，即使在我們的生命風浪中，祂也隨時準備著接近我們，帶給我們平安。當我們面臨艱難時，要記得轉向主，祂會以祂的方式親自安慰並扶持我們。
q: 當您遇到生命中的風浪時，是否能夠認出主的同在並放心信靠祂？您是否願意在困難中緊緊依靠主，相信祂會在適當的時候賜下平安？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您在我們的困境中從未離棄，無論風浪多大，您都與我們同在。求您賜給我們信心，能夠在困難中辨認您的同在，並接受您賜下的平安。幫助我們在每一個挑戰中更加信靠您，不再懷疑，堅定地依靠您。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,
and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick, on their mats, to where they heard he was.

Wherever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.
b: 這段經文記錄了耶穌在革尼撒勒所行的醫治神蹟。眾人一認出耶穌，就迫不及待地把各地的病人帶到祂面前，盼望他們能得到醫治。他們對耶穌充滿信心，相信只要摸到祂的衣裳繸子就能痊癒。耶穌的同在帶來了滿溢的醫治能力，祂無條件地接納並醫治每一位帶著信心前來的人，展現了祂對人無盡的愛與憐憫。
這段經文提醒我們，耶穌的愛和大能從不受限於任何地方或時間。無論我們的傷痛有多深，病痛有多重，祂的醫治始終都在我們身邊。這群人對耶穌的信心啟發了我們：即使只是短暫的接觸，我們也能因信而領受祂的醫治。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，當我們心靈或身體有需要時，不要害怕或遲疑，帶著信心來到主面前。祂樂意接納我們，賜下醫治與平安。無論是多小的信心，祂都看重，並且願意將祂的大能彰顯在我們的生命中。
q: 在生活的困境中，您是否願意以信心來到主面前，觸摸祂的醫治大能？有什麼生命的痛苦或掙扎是您願意交託給祂的？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您在我們的傷痛中賜下耶穌基督成為我們的醫治者。求您幫助我們以單純的信心來到您的面前，無論我們面臨何種困難，都相信您的愛與大能足以醫治一切。願我們的生命成為您恩典的見證。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.
Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, they found fault.
(For the Pharisees and all the Jews don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.

They don’t eat when they come from the marketplace unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things, which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)
The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why don’t your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?”
b: 在這段經文中，法利賽人和文士對耶穌的門徒沒有遵守古人的傳統，感到疑惑並提出質疑。對他們而言，這些外在的清潔規矩和傳統極其重要，象徵著他們的屬靈潔淨與對律法的堅持。然而，耶穌不在乎這些外在的清潔儀式，祂更加關心人內心的真實敬拜與純潔。在他們眼中，不洗手似乎是違反律法，但耶穌卻讓我們看見，神更看重的是內心的態度，而非形式化的宗教行為。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，不要僅僅專注於外在的儀式，而忽略了內在的心靈潔淨。真正的信仰不是表面的行為，而是內心對神的順服和真誠。我們可能常常因為習慣和傳統而忽略了信仰的本質。主耶穌邀請我們放下那些無意義的外在規條，回歸到與祂的真實關係中。
q: 在您的信仰生活中，有沒有哪些習慣或規矩是您過於注重外表而忽略了內心？今天，您可以如何更真誠地來到神面前？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您提醒我們信仰的真正核心在於我們的內心，而非外在的形式。求您賜給我們一顆清潔的心，使我們的敬拜和順服都是出於真心，討您的喜悅。願我們的生命每一天都因著與您真實的關係而被更新。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
But they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
“For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
He said to them, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban,” ’ ” that is to say, given to God,
“then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
b: 這段經文讓我們看見耶穌對法利賽人和文士的責備，是因為他們在信仰上拘泥於外在的傳統，而忽略了信仰的真諦。耶穌引用先知以賽亞的話，指出這些人雖然用嘴唇尊敬神，但心卻遠離了祂。他們崇尚人的遺傳，甚至將人的遺傳等同於神的律法，以致他們的敬拜成了空虛無效的形式。
特別是在第11至13節中，耶穌揭露了他們扭曲「孝敬父母」的誡命，以「各耳板」的制度來避開對父母的責任。「各耳板」是一種將財產獻給神的方式，表面上是虔誠的捐獻，實際上卻使人可以以「財產已奉獻給神」為藉口，免去對父母的扶養責任。這種行為看似「屬靈」，但本質上卻是一種虛假的虔誠，是在利用宗教為自己開脫責任。耶穌指出，這樣的行為是「廢了神的道」，因為他們把人的傳統看得比神的律法還重要。
耶穌在這段話中，不僅批評了當時宗教領袖的假冒為善，也提醒我們要警惕自己在信仰上的形式化和表面化。我們是否有時候也用「屬靈」的藉口來規避我們的責任？是否在外表上看起來敬虔，實際上卻在心裡遠離了神？真正的信仰不是遵循人的傳統，而是順服神的誡命，讓我們的心在神面前真誠、悔改，並且行出祂所喜悅的公義和慈愛。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，不要拘泥於外在的形式或傳統，而忽視了信仰的核心。信仰的本質是心靈的真誠，是對神的愛和順服，而不是為了人的認可而保持表面的虔誠。上帝希望我們在日常生活中真實地活出信仰，真正尊重和遵行祂的誡命，並且以愛來服事祂和他人，尤其是在家庭中彰顯孝道和愛的責任。
q: 在您的生活中，有沒有某些習慣或行為，只是出於人的遺傳或習慣，而非神的誡命？如何讓神的話語成為您生活中真正的標準，使信仰的每一部分都能榮耀神並彰顯祂的愛？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌提醒我們信仰的真諦。求您讓我們擺脫一切表面的虔誠，能夠用真誠的心敬拜您，讓我們的行為與信仰一致。願我們在生活中真實地彰顯您的愛和公義，特別是在家庭中活出您對我們的呼召。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: He called all the multitude to himself, and said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.
He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,
because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, making all foods clean?”
He said, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”
b: 耶穌在這段經文中教導我們，真正能使人污穢的不在於外在的事物，而是來自內心的動機與思想。祂呼籲眾人聆聽並明白這重要的教訓：從外面進入的東西無法使人污穢，因為那不會影響人的心靈，最終只是被身體排出。然而，真正使人污穢的是從內心深處出來的邪惡，這些來自心靈的惡念才是罪的根源。
當門徒私下問耶穌這比喻的含義時，祂解釋說，從外面進來的食物不能污穢人，因為那不進入心靈，只進入身體並最終排出體外。耶穌透過這段教訓向我們揭示，食物和外在的行為並不是信仰的核心，反而，內心的動機和思想才是上帝看重的。我們的心靈如果充滿了惡念、貪婪、詭詐、驕傲等罪惡，這些內在的腐敗會影響我們的行為，成為真實的污穢。
耶穌列舉了許多從人心裡發出的惡念，如苟合、偷盜、凶殺、姦淫等，提醒我們警惕內心的敗壞。這些內在的罪惡不僅破壞了我們與上帝的關係，也破壞了我們與他人的關係。耶穌的教導告訴我們，信仰不只是外表的潔淨或遵循規條，而是內心的潔淨。我們需要定時審查自己的心靈，讓神的真理和愛潔淨我們的內心，遠離一切會污穢我們的邪念。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，信仰的本質在於內心的純潔與真誠。外在的行為雖然重要，但若內心充滿邪念和不義，那麼一切的表面功夫也無法掩蓋內心的污穢。真正的信仰生活應當是由內而外的潔淨，從心靈深處開始，並讓每一個行為都顯出神的榮美和公義。
q: 在日常生活中，是否有一些負面的想法或情緒時常在內心出現？如何透過禱告和聖靈的幫助潔淨自己的心靈，使生活更加和神的心意一致？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您讓我們認識到內心純潔的重要。求您幫助我們時刻檢視自己的心靈，讓您的愛和真理潔淨我們，去除一切的邪念，使我們能夠從內心深處敬拜您。求您讓我們在行為上與信仰一致，成為您所喜悅的器皿。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: From there he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.
For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.
Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.
b: 這段經文記錄了耶穌在推羅和希頓的地區，遇見一位求助的婦人。這位婦人是外邦人，她的女兒被污鬼附身，她深知耶穌能夠醫治她的女兒。儘管耶穌起初的回答看似冷漠，但她的信心和謙卑使她得到了一個美好的結果。
耶穌用「狗」來形容外邦人，這是針對當時猶太人對外邦人的看法，意在測試婦人的信心。她的回應顯示出她的信心和謙卑，知道即使是最微小的恩典也足夠她女兒得醫治。耶穌因她的信心而答應了她的請求，並且女兒立即被解救。
這個故事提醒我們，無論我們來自何處，只要有真誠的信心，神就會垂聽我們的祈禱。耶穌的憐憫和能力不受任何限制，祂能夠滿足我們的需要，解決我們的困境。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，真正的信心和謙卑能夠突破一切障礙。無論我們的背景或狀況如何，只要我們來到神面前，誠心尋求，神必會回應我們的禱告，賜下恩典和醫治。
q: 在您的生命中，有哪些方面您需要更多的信心和謙卑？如何在困境中學習這位婦人的信心，並相信神會垂聽您的禱告？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌基督，讓我們看到信心和謙卑的力量。求您幫助我們在面對困難時，能夠持守信心，並謙卑地來到您面前尋求您的幫助。願我們的信心如同這位婦人一樣，無論處於何種境地，都能得到您的回應與醫治。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.
He took him aside from the multitude, privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue.
Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!”  that is, “Be opened!”
Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.
He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.
They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear, and the mute speak!”
b: 這段經文描述了耶穌醫治一位聾啞人的奇蹟。耶穌在加利利海附近遇到這位需要幫助的男子，他的朋友們帶著他來求耶穌的醫治。耶穌的醫治方式異常獨特，祂用唾沫噴在男子的耳朵上，然後用手按他的舌頭，最後祂對他說「以法他！」，這句話意味著「開了！」。
耶穌的行為充滿了深意，這些動作和言語象徵著對於身體和靈性的重生與醫治。耶穌的嘆息表達了對人類痛苦的憐憫和關懷。醫治後，男子的耳朵立刻開啟，舌頭也能說話，顯示出耶穌的神力和愛心。
儘管耶穌要求不傳揚這件事，但人們的驚奇和對耶穌工作的讚美，讓消息不斷擴散。耶穌的醫治不僅僅是身體上的改變，更是神的國度在地上的顯現。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，耶穌能夠醫治我們的身體和心靈，祂的力量超越我們的理解。無論我們面臨何種困境，耶穌的能力都能帶來改變。這段經文也提醒我們，神的奇蹟常常會引起人的讚美和見證，即使耶穌的旨意是低調的，祂的工作仍然會顯示出祂的榮耀。
q: 在您的生活中，有哪些需要神醫治的地方？如何學習這位聾啞人的信心，並相信神的能力能夠帶來改變和更新？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌基督，讓我們見證了祂的醫治和奇蹟。求您幫助我們在生活中信靠祢的能力，並在困難中尋求祢的幫助。願我們的心靈和身體都能得到祢的醫治，並在生活中見證祢的榮耀。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself, and said to them,
“I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.
If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”
His disciples answered him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”
He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.
They had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.
They ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.
Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
b: 這段經文再次展現了耶穌對群眾的憐憫和供應。在眾人跟隨祂三天之後，耶穌深知他們的疲憊和飢餓，因此主動與門徒商量如何滿足他們的需求。門徒因身處荒野而感到束手無策，但耶穌沒有因環境的限制而退縮，而是藉著微薄的食物來彰顯神豐富的供應。

When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”
He said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting.”
b: 在這段經文中，我們看到一位父親因其兒子被污鬼附著而深受痛苦。當門徒無法趕出這鬼時，這位父親懷著無助的心情求助於耶穌。耶穌揭示了信心的重要性，告訴他「在信的人，凡事都能」。這句話觸動了父親的心，使他喊出「我信！但我信不足，求主幫助」。這真實的呼喊表達了人類在信心上的掙扎與有限，但也顯示出神的憐憫與慈愛，祂不拒絕這父親的求助，並藉著信心的禱告將他的兒子從捆綁中釋放出來。
耶穌最終成功趕出污鬼，使孩子得到釋放和醫治。這過程中，門徒暗暗問耶穌為何自己無法趕出鬼，耶穌告訴他們「非用禱告（有古卷加禁食），這一類的鬼總不能出來」。這提醒我們禱告的重要性，禱告是神賜給我們的屬靈力量，使我們在困難和試煉中得以得勝。透過禱告，我們能接觸神的能力，而非單憑自己的力量去面對靈界的挑戰。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，信心和禱告是我們在屬靈戰爭中的武器。我們可能在信心上有所不足，但只要我們願意誠實地面對並向神呼求，祂會加添我們的力量，帶領我們勝過一切的難處。這段經文不僅展示了耶穌的能力，也提醒我們要時刻依靠神的同在，在每一個挑戰面前勇敢站立。
q: 在面對生命中的困難時，您是否有足夠的信心與禱告？您願意向神呼求，求祂幫助您增強信心，使您能勝過挑戰嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜給我們信心的力量，並教導我們禱告的寶貴。求您增強我們的信心，使我們在挑戰中能夠完全信靠您，也求您賜我們禱告的靈，使我們的心緊連於您，能夠得著從您而來的能力和智慧。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: They went out from there, and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it.
For he was teaching his disciples, and said to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”
But they didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.
He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them, “What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”
But they were silent, for they had disputed with one another on the way about who was the greatest.
He sat down, and called the twelve; and he said to them, “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”
He took a little child, and set him in the middle of them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,
“Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”
b: 這段經文揭示了耶穌對門徒的深刻教導和祂對真正偉大的定義。耶穌在預告自己的受難和復活時，門徒卻未能理解這重要的教導，並且不敢詢問。這顯示了他們的恐懼和對耶穌使命的模糊理解。門徒在路上的爭論也暴露了他們對權力和地位的渴望，這與耶穌的教導形成了鮮明的對比。
耶穌的教導顯示，真正的領袖不是以權力和地位來衡量，而是以謙卑和服務為基礎。耶穌讓一個小孩站在他們中間，並且抱著他，強調接待和關愛這樣的人。當時的小孩在社會中地位低微，無法為自己爭取什麼，但耶穌卻用小孩作為榜樣，教導門徒真正的偉大來自於對所有人的關懷和服務。
這段經文提醒我們，在現代社會中，我們也應該以謙卑和服務為導向，尋求在他人生活中發揮積極的影響力。這不僅僅是表現在對小孩或弱勢群體的關愛，也包括在日常生活中以謙卑的心態對待每一個人。我們的目標是像耶穌一樣，成為眾人的僕人，而不是追求世俗的地位和榮耀。
q: 在您的生活中，有哪些地方您可以更好地實踐謙卑和服務？如何具體地在生活中關懷和幫助那些需要幫助的人？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您透過耶穌的教導提醒我們真正的偉大在於謙卑和服務。求您幫助我們在生活中實踐這些原則，無論是在家庭、工作還是社區中，都能夠以謙卑的心對待他人，關愛每一個需要幫助的人。願我們的生命能夠活出真正的領袖特質，以愛和服務為他人。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone who doesn’t follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow us.”
But Jesus said, “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against us is on our side.
For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.
Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.
If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna,  into the unquenchable fire,
‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna,  into the fire that will never be quenched—
‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire,
‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.
Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌針對門徒在排斥不屬於他們的人的行為提出了教導。約翰告訴耶穌，他們曾經禁止一個非門徒的人成為耶穌名下的施行者，因為這人不隨他們的隊伍。然而，耶穌告訴他們，不應該禁止他人，因為任何用耶穌名義行神跡的人，無法輕看耶穌的事工。
耶穌進一步警告，任何使信徒跌倒的，將會面臨嚴厲的懲罰。這裡用“把大磨石拴在脖子上，投在海裡”來形容，強調使人跌倒的罪行是極其嚴重的。接著，耶穌使用了強烈的比喻，告誡門徒如果手、腳或眼使他們跌倒，就必須忍痛割舍，因為這些肢體雖小，但關乎永生的重大選擇。這些比喻提醒我們，任何會妨礙我們靈命成長的事物，都應該及早擺脫，以免因為小小的失敗而被丟棄在地獄。
最後，耶穌提到鹽的比喻，鹽代表了基督徒生活中的品德和價值。失去鹽分的鹽是無用的，因此我們的生活應該充滿基督的鹽分，即充滿和睦與善良，才能真正地反映出基督的樣式。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，在信仰生活中，我們要彼此包容和接納，不應排斥其他為主事工而努力的人。同時，對我們的靈命要保持警覺，及時修正任何使我們跌倒的因素，並且在生活中彰顯基督的品德。
q: 在您的生活中，是否有某些行為或習慣使您跌倒？如何修正這些行為，並保持基督徒生活的鹽分？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您提醒我們要以包容和愛心對待他人，並且在生活中保持警覺，防止任何使我們跌倒的因素。求您幫助我們在信仰中成為有鹽的生命，反映出基督的品德與價值。願我們在日常生活中，能夠以愛心和和睦為主，活出真正的基督徒生命。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.
Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
He answered, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”
But Jesus said to them, “For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.
For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”
In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.
He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌教導關於婚姻的真理。法利賽人來試探耶穌，詢問關於離婚的問題。這個問題不僅是法律上的爭議，也是當時社會倫理的焦點。耶穌首先回顧了摩西律法的規定，摩西允許人寫休書，使妻子可以離婚。但耶穌指出，這是因為人心硬，而非神原本的計劃。
耶穌回到創造的根本，強調神從起初創造人是男是女，婚姻的本質是讓夫妻成為一體。耶穌的教導強調婚姻的神聖性和不可分割性，表明神所配合的婚姻不應該被人拆散。這表明婚姻的真正意義是神所設立的合一，不僅是法律上的契約，更是靈性的結合。
當門徒在家中詢問耶穌關於這個問題時，耶穌進一步解釋，離婚再婚會導致奸淫，因為這違背了神對婚姻的設立和目的。這提醒我們婚姻的關係應受到尊重，應該努力維護和修復，而不是輕易地結束。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，婚姻是神所設立的神聖聯合，應該尊重和珍惜。離婚不是神的原意，我們應該致力於在婚姻中保持合一，並在遇到困難時尋求神的幫助和指引。
q: 在您的婚姻或關係中，有哪些方面需要改進或修復？如何在這些方面尋求神的幫助和指引，維護婚姻的合一？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您設立婚姻的美好計劃。求您幫助我們尊重和珍惜婚姻中的合一，並在面對困難時，尋求您的幫助和智慧。願我們在婚姻中能夠彰顯您的愛和恩典，並且努力維護婚姻的神聖性。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
He took them in his arms, and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
b: 這段經文記錄了耶穌對小孩子的愛和對神國的教導。當時有人帶小孩子來見耶穌，希望祂能為他們祝福。然而，門徒因為認為小孩子不重要，便責備那些人。耶穌見狀，對門徒表示憤怒，並告訴他們應當讓小孩子到祂那裡來，因為在神的國裡，正是這樣的人。
耶穌的教導告訴我們，神國的特質在於像小孩子那樣的純真和依賴。小孩子的心靈是純潔和單純的，這種特質正是神所喜悅的。耶穌強調，只有像小孩子那樣，帶著單純的信心和依賴，才能進入神的國度。
耶穌抱起小孩子，為他們按手祝福，顯示出對他們的關愛和重視。這不僅僅是一個祝福的行為，也是對所有人的提醒——神的愛是無條件的，無論我們的年齡、地位如何，神都願意接納和祝福我們。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，進入神國需要單純的信心和依賴，像小孩子那樣對神懷有信任和依賴。我們應該學習擁有這種單純的心靈，並且接納和祝福周圍的每一個人。

pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您對我們的愛和關懷。求您幫助我們像小孩子一樣，帶著純真的信心和依賴來親近您。願我們在生活中能夠學習您的愛，並且以愛心祝福他人。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’ ”
He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”

Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.
b: 這段經文描述了一位富有的年輕人向耶穌請教如何得著永生的故事。這位年輕人對耶穌提出問題，渴望得到永生。耶穌先是提醒他，除了神以外，沒有真正的良善，並引用了律法中的幾條誡命來檢視他的行為。這位年輕人回答說自己從小就遵守了這些誡命。
耶穌看見他的真誠和良善，對他充滿了愛。然後，耶穌提出了一個挑戰：要他變賣所有的財產，分給窮人，然後跟隨祂。這不僅僅是對他的要求，更是一個測試，來檢驗他是否願意將財富和地上的依賴放在一旁，完全依靠神。
年輕人聽見這話，心中充滿了灰心，因為他的財富使他難以放下。這反映了對物質的依賴可能阻礙我們追求神的心志和永生。耶穌的要求表明，真正跟隨祂需要全心全意地將地上的一切放在神的手中，並以神的國度為首要。
上帝透過這段經文告訴我們，信仰不僅僅是外在的遵守誡命，更是內心對神完全的依賴和信任。我們需要檢視自己是否在物質和世俗的牽絆中，願意完全跟隨神。
q: 在您的生活中，有哪些物質或世俗的牽絆影響了您對神的跟隨？如何學習放下這些依賴，讓神的國度成為您生命的首要？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您對我們的愛和恩典。求您幫助我們在追求您的過程中，願意放下世上的一切依賴，全心全意地跟隨您。願我們在生活中能夠以您的國度為最重要的目標，並且忠心地依靠您的供應。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Jesus looked around, and said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”
The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”
Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”
Peter began to tell him, “Behold, we have left all, and have followed you.”

Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,
but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time: houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last; and the last first.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌強調了財富對進入天國的障礙。耶穌告訴門徒，擁有財富的人進入天國是非常困難的。這是因為財富容易使人心思偏離神的國度，並且造成對世俗的過度依賴。門徒對此感到驚訝，因為他們普遍認為富有的人應當更容易得到神的祝福。
耶穌指出，靠自己是無法得救的，唯有神的能力才能改變一切。他用「駱駝穿針」的比喻，來形容這一困難，顯示神的救恩是超乎我們理解的奇妙工作。耶穌鼓勵門徒，即使一切看似不可能，神依然能使之成為可能。
彼得提到他們已經為了跟從耶穌而捨棄了許多。耶穌回應說，凡是為祂和福音捨去的，必在今世得到百倍的祝福，並在來世獲得永生。這不僅是對門徒的應許，也是對所有跟隨祂的人的應許。耶穌提醒我們，即使付出代價，神的回報是遠超我們所能想像的。
上帝透過這段經文提醒我們，雖然進入神的國度可能需要捨棄一些世俗的依賴，但神會賜下超乎想像的祝福和永生。我們需要檢視自己是否把財富和世俗的價值觀放在首位，並學習依靠神的能力來達成祂的旨意。

pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下永生的應許和豐盛的祝福。求您幫助我們在追求您的過程中，能夠捨棄世俗的依賴，將您放在我們生命中的首位。願我們在生活中不斷地依靠您的能力，並且經歷您奇妙的祝福。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.

v: Some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They asked him, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’
There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.
The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;
and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”
Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?
For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
But about the dead, that they are raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
b: 這段經文記載了撒都該人對耶穌提出關於復活的問題。他們提出了一個關於婚姻和復活的難題，試圖用這個問題來揭示復活的荒謬。耶穌回應他們，指出他們的錯誤，並且重新解釋了復活的真理。
耶穌指出，復活的生命不再受到地上的婚姻制度限制，因為在復活後，人將像天使一樣存在。祂引用了摩西在荊棘中所說的經文，證明神是活人的神，從而指出死人復活的真理。
這段經文提醒我們，對神的真理的理解需要神的啟示和靈的幫助。我們需要透過聖經和神的話語來明白復活的真理，以及神的大能。
q: 您對復活的真理有什麼樣的理解？這些理解如何影響您的信仰生活？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您透過耶穌的教導讓我們明白復活的真理。求您幫助我們在信仰上更深地認識您的大能，並且在生活中持守這些真理。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。
